name: Rohan Shah
current_role: Co-founder and Chief Revenue Officer, Extend (product protection / extended warranty platform, San Francisco)
profile: Stanford 2014 graduate who co-founded Extend in 2019 with Woody Levin and others; the company lets merchants offer extended warranties and protection plans and handles claims, with customers such as Peloton, iRobot and Logitech. He is listed as Founder & CRO / head of partnerships. Not to be confused with Extend (paywithextend, virtual cards, CEO Andrew Jamison).
interesting_fact: Named to Forbes 30 Under 30 in 2020 for co-founding Extend, which grew to 100+ full-time employees in under two years.
deep_cut_fact: His first startup after Stanford, which sold to startups, didn't work out; he then became a product lead in BCG's Digital Ventures group to build skills before co-founding Extend. His parents are both entrepreneurs who started a company together in 1987. Quote: 'I was always the best at learning by doing.'
notes: Hurun's 'Extend' here is the warranty company (extend.com), not the fintech paywithextend.com. NYSE TV lists him as 'Extend Founder & CRO' (https://tv.nyse.com/ceos-leaders/videos/extend-founder-cro-rohan-shah). No published personal contact found.

name: Jerome Ternynck
current_role: Founder of SmartRecruiters (acquired by SAP, closed Sept 2025); MarketScreener lists him as Chairman since April 2023; Rebecca Carr is now SmartRecruiters CEO
profile: French entrepreneur who spent a decade in recruiting software, founding Lumesse (formerly in the UK) in 1999 and serving as CEO until 2010. He moved from Paris to San Francisco in 2010 and founded SmartRecruiters, a talent-acquisition SaaS used by 4,000+ organisations, which SAP agreed to acquire in August 2025.
interesting_fact: SAP announced the acquisition of SmartRecruiters on Aug 1, 2025 and completed it on Sept 11, 2025, planning to integrate it with SuccessFactors while keeping it available standalone.
deep_cut_fact: After moving from Paris to San Francisco in 2010 he raised $1M in seed money; SmartRecruiters launched in summer 2011 as a free job-posting app and didn't launch its first paid product until May 2014. His stated goal: 'I wanted to make hiring a quality business, and I wanted to give people a job they loved.'

public_contacts.value: Interview: 'Itw Jérôme Ternynck, CEO & Founder SmartRecruiters' (French Tech San Francisco podcast)

notes: Post-acquisition role unclear; best route likely via SmartRecruiters/SAP press or LinkedIn. The podcast entry is a past interview, not his own channel.
